item.text: The Royal Commission into Defence and Veteran Suicide was asked to identify systemic problems and propose ways to prevent suicide and suicidality among current and former ADF members.
item.support:
This Royal Commission was tasked with identifying systemic problems and proposing 
systemic solutions

item.text: It examined cultural, structural and systemic issues across the ADF, Defence and the Department of Veterans’ Affairs.
item.support:
We 
were directed to focus on cultural, structural and systemic issues

item.text: The Commission found that institutional problems in Defence and the Department of Veterans’ Affairs contributed to persistently high levels of suicide and suicidality.
item.support:
Our inquiry has found that numerous institutional drivers within Defence and DVA 
contribute to the persistently high rates of suicide and suicidality

item.text: Its 122 recommendations address harm prevention, early intervention, coordination of support, institutional capability and stronger oversight.
item.support: A full list of our 122 recommendations is outlined in the following section of this report.

item.quote:
Our inquiry has found that numerous institutional drivers within Defence and DVA 
contribute to the persistently high rates of suicide and suicidality among serving and 
ex-serving ADF members.

There is no comprehensive oversight of the defence and veteran ecosystem and its 
performance in relation to suicide prevention.
